rationale: The Linux job repeatedly runs `apt-get update && apt-get install` on every run with no dependency cache, which is repeated dependency fetching. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (dependency_cache) is evidence-supported for caching dependency downloads while keeping installation and all required tests. Adding an `actions/cache@v4` step for `/var/cache/apt/archives`, keyed on `runner.os`, preserves every build and test step unchanged, adds no secrets, privileged actions, publishing/deployment, or new external network access, and does not weaken permissions. Bazel patterns do not apply because the CI workflow does not invoke Bazel; custom timeouts lack representative successful-duration history (recent runs are all failures) and risk false timeouts on long cross-platform builds; cancel-stale conflicts with the release/attestation work in distcheck; and the Windows matrix explicitly sets fail-fast: false.
